title: Spec: Rewrite Downstream Marts for the Unpivoted fct_compute_offers
body:
# Spec: Rewrite Downstream Marts for the Unpivoted `fct_compute_offers`

## Problem Statement

The `fct_compute_offers` fact table was unpivoted (ADR 003): its grain changed from `(offer_id, valid_from)` to `(offer_id, valid_from, tariff_tier_skey)`, and the 14+ pivoted cost/profit columns were replaced with generic `cost_usd_per_hr`, `profit_usd_per_hr`, `cost_per_tflop_usd`, and `profit_per_tflop_usd` columns. The four downstream marts (`mart_arbitrage_opportunities`, `mart_best_offers_by_gpu`, `mart_profitability_trends`, `mart_gpu_model_summary`) and their schema documentation still reference the old pivoted columns and the old `dim_electricity_tariff_schedule` dimension name. These marts will fail to build and must be rewritten to consume the unpivoted fact table.

## Solution

Rewrite the four downstream marts to operate on the unpivoted `fct_compute_offers` fact table at offer×tier grain, and update `marts/schema.yml` to document the new columns, grains, and tests. Each mart carries the tariff tier context (`tariff_tier_skey`, `consumer_category`, `tariff_window_type`, `tariff_block_number`) alongside the generic cost/profit metrics.

## User Stories

1. As an arbitrage analyst, I want `mart_arbitrage_opportunities` to expose one row per (offer, tariff tier), so that I can see the best offer for each tier rather than only the business-high tier.
2. As an arbitrage analyst, I want each offer ranked within its (offer_type, tariff tier) group by that tier's `profit_per_tflop_usd`, so that rank 1 is the best opportunity for that tier.
3. As an arbitrage analyst, I want the tier context (`consumer_category`, `tariff_window_type`, `tariff_block_number`) carried on each row, so that I can filter and group by tier without joining back to the dimension.
4. As an arbitrage analyst, I want the generic `cost_usd_per_hr`, `profit_usd_per_hr`, `cost_per_tflop_usd`, and `profit_per_tflop_usd` columns on each row, so that I can compare tiers directly.
5. As a GPU procurement analyst, I want `mart_best_offers_by_gpu` to expose the best offer per (GPU variant, tariff tier), so that I can see the best GPU per tier rather than only under the business-high tariff.
6. As a GPU procurement analyst, I want the best-offer selection per (GPU variant, tariff tier) to be by that tier's `profit_usd_per_hr / number_of_gpus`, so that the selection is consistent with the tier being evaluated.
7. As a GPU procurement analyst, I want per-GPU normalized cost/profit metrics (`cost_per_gpu_usd_per_hr`, `profit_per_gpu_usd_per_hr`) on each row, so that I can compare offers with different GPU counts.
8. As a trends analyst, I want `mart_profitability_trends` to keep the tariff window schedule join, so that I can still analyze profitability during scheduled high/low tariff hours.
9. As a trends analyst, I want the scheduled window labeled distinctly (e.g. `scheduled_tariff_window`) from the tier's own `tariff_window_type`, so that I can distinguish "when the tariff is scheduled high" from "which tier this row represents".
10. As a trends analyst, I want hourly aggregates of `profit_usd_per_hr` and `profit_per_tflop_usd` (avg/min/max) grouped by GPU attributes, scheduled window, and tier context, so that I can see profitability trends per tier over time.
11. As a GPU model analyst, I want `mart_gpu_model_summary` to group by (GPU variant, tariff tier) with a single `pct_profitable` column, so that I can see the share of profitable offers per tier per GPU model.
12. As a GPU model analyst, I want the summary to retain `pct_verified`, `pct_available`, `avg_reliability_score`, `avg_kwh_per_tflop`, `avg_revenue_per_gpu_usd_per_hr`, and `last_seen_at`, so that host quality and efficiency context is preserved.
13. As a data platform engineer, I want `marts/schema.yml` updated to document the new offer×tier grain and generic columns, so that the data catalog reflects reality.
14. As a data platform engineer, I want the unique-key tests updated to include `tariff_tier_skey`, so that the offer×tier grain is enforced.
15. As a data platform engineer, I want singular grain tests asserting exactly 7 rows per offer snapshot (and per GPU variant) in the marts, so that the unpivoted grain is verified end-to-end.
16. As a data platform engineer, I want the marts to build successfully against the unpivoted fact table, so that the dbt DAG is green.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Grain**: All four marts operate at offer×tier grain (one row per (offer, tariff tier)), consistent with the unpivoted fact table.
- **`mart_arbitrage_opportunities`**: Keep the current-offers and available-offers filters (verified, rentable, unrented, positive tflops/revenue/tdp). Rank within each `(offer_type, tariff_tier_skey)` by that tier's `profit_per_tflop_usd`, preserving the existing tiebreakers (reliability desc, tdp asc, pcie bandwidth desc, gpu bandwidth desc, valid_from desc). Carry tier context and generic cost/profit columns.
- **`mart_best_offers_by_gpu`**: Keep the current-offers and available-offers filters. Pick the best offer per `(offer_type, gpu_architecture, gpu_model_name, gpu_memory_gb, tariff_tier_skey)` by that tier's `profit_usd_per_hr / number_of_gpus`, keeping `rn = 1`. Per-GPU metrics become generic (`cost_per_gpu_usd_per_hr`, `profit_per_gpu_usd_per_hr`, `cost_per_tflop_usd`, `profit_per_tflop_usd`) plus tier context.
- **`mart_profitability_trends`**: Keep the schedule join, but to the renamed `dim_electricity_tariff_window_schedule`, joining on `day_of_week`/`hour`/`valid_from`/`valid_to`. Alias the scheduled window as `scheduled_tariff_window` to avoid collision with the fact's `tariff_window_type`. Group by hour + GPU attributes + `scheduled_tariff_window` + tier context (`tariff_tier_skey`, `consumer_category`, `tariff_window_type`, `tariff_block_number`). Aggregate `profit_usd_per_hr` and `profit_per_tflop_usd` (avg/min/max) plus `avg_revenue_usd_per_hr` and `offer_count`.
- **`mart_gpu_model_summary`**: Group by `(offer_type, gpu_architecture, gpu_model_name, tflops_per_gpu, gpu_memory_gb, tariff_tier_skey)`. Single `pct_profitable` column (share of current offers with `profit_usd_per_hr > 0` for that tier), plus tier context, `pct_verified`, `pct_available`, `avg_reliability_score`, `avg_kwh_per_tflop`, `avg_revenue_per_gpu_usd_per_hr`, `last_seen_at`.
- **`marts/schema.yml`**: Rewrite all four model definitions — update grains, unique-key tests (add `tariff_tier_skey`; for trends add `scheduled_tariff_window` + `tariff_tier_skey`), and replace all 7-tier column docs with the generic tier-scoped columns.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam**: The dbt test layer on the marts themselves — the highest seam available. The marts are the external behavior; tests assert their contract directly.
- **Schema tests** in `marts/schema.yml`:
  - `unique_combination_of_columns` updated to reflect the offer×tier grain (add `tariff_tier_skey`; for trends add `scheduled_tariff_window` + `tariff_tier_skey`).
  - `not_null` on the new tier-context columns (`tariff_tier_skey`, `consumer_category`, `tariff_window_type`).
  - `accepted_values` on `tariff_window_type` (`low`/`high`) and `scheduled_tariff_window` (`low`/`high`).
- **Singular tests** in `src/transform/tests/`:
  - `mart_arbitrage_opportunities` has exactly 7 rows per offer snapshot.
  - `mart_best_offers_by_gpu` has exactly 7 rows per GPU variant.
- **Prior art**: `assert_fct_compute_offers_unpivoted_grain.sql` and `assert_fct_compute_offers_cost_profit_calculation.sql` already follow this pattern for the fact table.

## Out of Scope

- Changes to the fact table, dimensions, staging, or intermediate models.
- Changes to the ingest/refine layers or the EVN tariff seeds.
- Re-pivoting any mart back to 7-tier columns.
- Changes to the `dim_electricity_tariff_window_schedule` dimension itself.

## Further Notes

- The `dim_electricity_tariff_schedule` model was renamed to `dim_electricity_tariff_window_schedule`; the trends mart must reference the new name.
- The fact's tier context column `tariff_window_type` and the scheduled window column must be aliased distinctly to avoid a column collision in the trends mart.
- This spec follows ADR 003 (Unpivot `fct_compute_offers` by Tariff Tier), which is accepted.
